issue.title: Improve inferring the "final" `static` type when calling static methods inside a different class

labels.name: release:fix
labels.description: The PR will be included in 'Fixes' section of the release notes

repository.name: psalm
repository.description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

issue.body:
fixes #8200

After some insane debugging and trying to wrap my head around it, I found the reason it behaves improperly.

When calling a static method of some class, there are two possibilities:
1. in the static method itself there might be something like `@return Collection<static>`, that means `static` is defined by the static method which we are calling.
2. this static method is parameterized with a template like `@return Collection<T>`, but the class which CALLS it can have something like `@return Collection<static>`. So `static` is defined by the CALLING code, not the CALLED. In this case, Psalm behaved incorrectly, because it always assumed only the 1st case.

I have to move the test case somewhere (for now it's a separate class), please give a hint.

Not really relevant, just curious. `Maybe` seems pretty clearly to be copying Rust's [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html), and you have `tryFrom` as well which also [comes from Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.TryFrom.html) (but maybe that name is actually taken from `BackedEnum::tryFrom`?).

I first learned about Maybe monad from Haskell (which is much older than Rust btw), and tryFrom() is just a common name I've seen in the wild, didn't actually know `try_from` is a standard trait in Rust - it means not only I think this pattern actually makes sense then.
Ah that makes sense, I haven't looked into Haskell too much, though I know Rust takes a lot of inspiration from it.
